tweets.text:
There's multiple variants of it, but on top of my head the setup had multiple layers:

1) Buying or selling before large blocks (risk-defining front-run).

2) Preferring trades against a recent position skew (they'll have to unwind front-run).

3) preffering entries after forced sellers or buyers (market drives back to the mean front-run).

4) Contextual relative strength. For example, when bad news gets absorbed (buyers are next, sellers lose their power).

Anyway, you can argue it's all front-run. When you're born, it's because you won a race. Thanks.
